texts.orig: 0.0 Boxed Warning and Contraindications

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: BOXED WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY: When pregnancy is detected, discontinue CardioNex as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the reninangiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus. ·

texts.orig: CONTRAINDICATIONS: ·
texts.text: CONTRAINDICATIONS: ·

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Concomitant use with ACE inhibitors is contraindicated due to angioedema risk. Allow a strict 36-hour washout period when switching from an ACE inhibitor to CardioNex. ◦
texts.text: Concomitant use with ACE inhibitors is contraindicated due to angioedema risk. Allow a strict 36-hour washout period when switching from an ACE inhibitor to CardioNex. ◦

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Contraindicated in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) requiring dialysis. ◦

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 1.1 Indications and Usage
texts.text: 1.1 Indications and Usage

texts.label: text
texts.orig: CardioNex is indicated ONLY to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adult patients with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, LVEF <= 40%).
texts.text: CardioNex is indicated ONLY to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adult patients with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, LVEF <= 40%).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Safety and efficacy have NOT been established in pediatric patients (< 18 years). ·
texts.text: Safety and efficacy have NOT been established in pediatric patients (< 18 years). ·

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Safety and efficacy have NOT been established in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF, LVEF > 40%). ·
texts.text: Safety and efficacy have NOT been established in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF, LVEF > 40%). ·

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 2.2 Dosing and Special Population Adjustments
texts.text: 2.2 Dosing and Special Population Adjustments

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Footnote *: In patients concurrently taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (such as itraconazole, ketoconazole, clarithromycin, or ritonavir), the maximum daily dose of CardioNex must NOT exceed 5mg once daily, even if renal function is normal (eGFR >= 30 mL/min).
texts.text: Footnote *: In patients concurrently taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (such as itraconazole, ketoconazole, clarithromycin, or ritonavir), the maximum daily dose of CardioNex must NOT exceed 5mg once daily, even if renal function is normal (eGFR >= 30 mL/min).

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 2.3 Administration
texts.text: 2.3 Administration

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Take CardioNex once daily at about the same time each day, with or without food.
texts.text: Take CardioNex once daily at about the same time each day, with or without food.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 5.1 Hyperkalemia
texts.text: 5.1 Hyperkalemia

texts.label: text
texts.orig: CardioNex can raise serum potassium. Check potassium before the first dose, 1 week after starting or changing the dose, and monthly for the first 3 months. Withhold treatment while serum potassium is above 5.5 mEq/L and restart only once it has returned to the normal range.
texts.text: CardioNex can raise serum potassium. Check potassium before the first dose, 1 week after starting or changing the dose, and monthly for the first 3 months. Withhold treatment while serum potassium is above 5.5 mEq/L and restart only once it has returned to the normal range.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 5.2 Symptomatic Hypotension
texts.text: 5.2 Symptomatic Hypotension

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Low blood pressure with dizziness or fainting is most likely in patients who are volume depleted or on high-dose diuretics. Correct volume depletion before the first dose. If hypotension occurs, lower the diuretic dose first, then consider a temporary interruption of CardioNex.
texts.text: Low blood pressure with dizziness or fainting is most likely in patients who are volume depleted or on high-dose diuretics. Correct volume depletion before the first dose. If hypotension occurs, lower the diuretic dose first, then consider a temporary interruption of CardioNex.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 5.3 Angioedema
texts.text: 5.3 Angioedema

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat has been reported. Stop CardioNex at once and do not restart it. Patients with a history of angioedema of any cause were not studied and should not receive CardioNex.
texts.text: Swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat has been reported. Stop CardioNex at once and do not restart it. Patients with a history of angioedema of any cause were not studied and should not receive CardioNex.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 5.4 Worsening Renal Function
texts.text: 5.4 Worsening Renal Function

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Serum creatinine may rise in the first weeks of treatment. Measure creatinine at baseline and after 1 to 2 weeks. A rise of more than 30% from baseline calls for a review of the diuretic dose and of other drugs that affect the kidneys.
texts.text: Serum creatinine may rise in the first weeks of treatment. Measure creatinine at baseline and after 1 to 2 weeks. A rise of more than 30% from baseline calls for a review of the diuretic dose and of other drugs that affect the kidneys.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 6.1 Clinical Trials Experience
texts.text: 6.1 Clinical Trials Experience

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In the placebo-controlled trial, 7.9% of patients on CardioNex and 6.1% on placebo stopped treatment because of an adverse reaction. Adverse reactions reported in at least 2% of patients and more often than placebo were dizziness (6.3% vs 3.9%), fatigue (4.4% vs 3.6%), cough (3.1% vs 2.8%) and nausea (2.5% vs 1.9%).
texts.text: In the placebo-controlled trial, 7.9% of patients on CardioNex and 6.1% on placebo stopped treatment because of an adverse reaction. Adverse reactions reported in at least 2% of patients and more often than placebo were dizziness (6.3% vs 3.9%), fatigue (4.4% vs 3.6%), cough (3.1% vs 2.8%) and nausea (2.5% vs 1.9%).

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 7.1 Potassium-Raising Drugs
texts.text: 7.1 Potassium-Raising Drugs

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Potassium supplements, potassiumsparing diuretics (spironolactone, eplerenone, amiloride) and salt substitutes that contain potassium increase the chance of hyperkalemia. Monitor serum potassium closely when any of these is used with CardioNex.
texts.text: Potassium supplements, potassiumsparing diuretics (spironolactone, eplerenone, amiloride) and salt substitutes that contain potassium increase the chance of hyperkalemia. Monitor serum potassium closely when any of these is used with CardioNex.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 7.2 Strong CYP3A4 Inducers
texts.text: 7.2 Strong CYP3A4 Inducers

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin and St John's wort lower CardioNex exposure by about 70% and may remove its benefit. Avoid using them together.
texts.text: Rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin and St John's wort lower CardioNex exposure by about 70% and may remove its benefit. Avoid using them together.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 8.1 Pregnancy
texts.text: 8.1 Pregnancy

texts.label: text
texts.orig: CardioNex can cause fetal harm when given during the second and third trimesters. Stop CardioNex as soon as pregnancy is detected and switch to a treatment that is safe in pregnancy. Women who could become pregnant should use effective contraception during treatment.
texts.text: CardioNex can cause fetal harm when given during the second and third trimesters. Stop CardioNex as soon as pregnancy is detected and switch to a treatment that is safe in pregnancy. Women who could become pregnant should use effective contraception during treatment.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 8.2 Lactation
texts.text: 8.2 Lactation

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It is not known whether cardionexib passes into human breast milk. In animal studies it was found in milk at levels close to those in plasma. Because of the risk of low blood pressure and high potassium in a breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment and for 5 days after the final dose.
texts.text: It is not known whether cardionexib passes into human breast milk. In animal studies it was found in milk at levels close to those in plasma. Because of the risk of low blood pressure and high potassium in a breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment and for 5 days after the final dose.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 8.4 Pediatric Use
texts.text: 8.4 Pediatric Use

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Safety and effectiveness in patients younger than 18 years have not been established.
texts.text: Safety and effectiveness in patients younger than 18 years have not been established.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 8.5 Geriatric Use
texts.text: 8.5 Geriatric Use

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Of the patients in the clinical trial, 38% were 65 or older and 14% were 75 or older. No overall differences in effectiveness were seen. Older patients had more dizziness and low blood pressure, so check blood pressure at each visit during the first month.
texts.text: Of the patients in the clinical trial, 38% were 65 or older and 14% were 75 or older. No overall differences in effectiveness were seen. Older patients had more dizziness and low blood pressure, so check blood pressure at each visit during the first month.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 8.6 Renal Impairment
texts.text: 8.6 Renal Impairment

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Exposure to cardionexib rises as kidney function falls. Starting and maintenance doses by eGFR are given in the dosing table in section 2.2. Patients on dialysis were not studied.
texts.text: Exposure to cardionexib rises as kidney function falls. Starting and maintenance doses by eGFR are given in the dosing table in section 2.2. Patients on dialysis were not studied.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 8.7 Hepatic Impairment
texts.text: 8.7 Hepatic Impairment

texts.label: text
texts.orig: No dose change is needed in mild or moderate hepatic impairment (ChildPugh A or B). CardioNex has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) and is not recommended there.
texts.text: No dose change is needed in mild or moderate hepatic impairment (ChildPugh A or B). CardioNex has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) and is not recommended there.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 10 Overdosage
texts.text: 10 Overdosage

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Low blood pressure is the most likely effect of an overdose. Give supportive care. Cardionexib is highly protein bound and is not removed by hemodialysis.
texts.text: Low blood pressure is the most likely effect of an overdose. Give supportive care. Cardionexib is highly protein bound and is not removed by hemodialysis.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 12.3 Pharmacokinetics
texts.text: 12.3 Pharmacokinetics

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Peak plasma levels are reached about 2 hours after a dose. The halflife is about 14 hours, so steady state is reached in 3 to 4 days. Cardionexib is cleared mainly by metabolism in the liver; less than 5% is excreted unchanged in urine.
texts.text: Peak plasma levels are reached about 2 hours after a dose. The halflife is about 14 hours, so steady state is reached in 3 to 4 days. Cardionexib is cleared mainly by metabolism in the liver; less than 5% is excreted unchanged in urine.
